solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Russian fellow, one taking leading position

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
the van is the front of an army or procession

explanation.surface: A Russian man is described as someone who likes to be out in front.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common Russian first name, the local equivalent of John.

clue.text: Occurrence in part of hospital involving police

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the police letters go inside

parts.note: taken as written
ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department
CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is a British police branch

explanation.surface: Something happens in a hospital department with the police involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'in part of hospital' as a location, but 'in' is a letter piece; 'involving' then wraps it and the ward around the police.
explanation.definitionFit: An incident is an event or happening, a synonym of occurrence.

clue.text: Public school head's banned pointed weapon

indicators.note: the head of the school's name is barred, so its first letter goes

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public (private fee-paying) school

explanation.surface: A school's headmaster has prohibited a sharp weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head's banned' reads as the headteacher forbidding something, but means the first letter is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed missile shot from a bow, the archer's weapon.

clue.text: Sailor — he isn't mad for alcoholic drink

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a standard abbreviation for a sailor

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters of the words he isn't have gone wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor is said not to be crazy about strong liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges the letters of 'he isn't'; 'for' is just a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A green, aniseed-flavoured spirit flavoured with wormwood, famously strong.

clue.text: Better half wanting everyone to join in dancing

indicators.note: joining in means entering the group, so the word for everyone goes inside
half here takes the first three of the six letters of Better

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A spouse, the better half, wants everybody to take part in the dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better half' reads as a spouse, but means half the word Better; 'to join in' puts the word for everyone inside it, and 'wanting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballet is a form of theatrical dancing, the noun used for the art.

clue.text: How planes might fly at air show, dope

definitions.text: How planes might fly at air show
definitions.meaning: aircraft at displays fly together in tight patterns
dope is slang for facts or inside knowledge

explanation.surface: Display flying meets a slangy request for the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is display flying in tight patterns; as one, it is facts or knowledge, slang dope.

clue.text: Suffer during most of term? I might

definitions.text: Suffer during most of term? I might

indicators.note: during means within, so the suffering word goes inside
most of means all but the last letter of the word term

parts.note: to ache is to suffer pain

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher admits to suffering through most of the school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims term to TER and 'during' puts ACHE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who works through school terms could well endure them, so the speaker is a schoolteacher.

clue.text: Listeners initially expecting another radio series

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: Audiences are eagerly awaiting another radio series.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the organs of hearing, so they are what listens.

clue.text: Artillerymen transported by beast of burden? That's sweet

indicators.note: the gunners are carried along inside the animal, so their letters sit within it

parts.note: a camel is a pack animal
RA, the Royal Artillery, is the British army's artillery regiment

explanation.surface: Gunners ride on a pack animal, and someone finds that charming.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy toffee-like confection is a kind of sweet, the British word for a candy.

clue.text: Email, I noted, confused old film star

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone muddled an email about a veteran screen star.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated term for a handsome actor idolised by fans who went to afternoon screenings.

clue.text: Talent shown by learner, just about

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for just surrounds the learner

parts.note: just means fair, equitable
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A beginner shows some ability, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just about' reads as 'roughly' but splits: 'just' is the word to be filled, 'about' says it goes round the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is a natural aptitude or knack, a synonym for talent.

clue.text: Sensible astronauts will want to come back here

definitions.text: astronauts will want to come back here
definitions.meaning: read literally, the phrase is the return journey from space to our planet

explanation.surface: Practical-minded astronauts look forward to coming home.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means practical and unpretentious; taken literally it is the journey home from orbit.

clue.text: Alienate sergeant somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some way or other, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: A sergeant somehow manages to alienate people.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to make someone unfriendly or distant, a synonym of alienate.

clue.text: Observing husband isn't in love

indicators.note: the husband's letter is absent from the word for love, so it is removed

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, so it means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone watching notices that a married man is not in love.
explanation.definitionFit: Noting means taking notice of or remarking on, a synonym of observing.

clue.text: Thinking process however needs time

parts.note: though means however, as in 'he came, though'

explanation.surface: Thinking things through takes time, after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought is the act or process of thinking, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Children I found in farm buildings

indicators.note: found in places the I within the word for farm buildings

parts.note: barns are farm buildings

explanation.surface: Someone discovers kids hiding in the barns.
explanation.walkthrough: Bairns is the Scottish and northern English word for children.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Scots and northern English word for youngsters or kids.

clue.text: Flock of geese flying along ultimately in strong wind

indicators.note: in places those final letters inside the wind

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

indicators.note: ultimately means take the final letter of each of the words flying and along

explanation.surface: Geese fly in formation against a strong wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes the last letters of 'flying' and 'along'; 'in' sets them within the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the collective noun for geese on the ground.

clue.text: Organise rep production featuring noted performer

indicators.note: a production here is something made from the given letters, so they are reworked

explanation.surface: A theatre is told to organise a repertory production starring a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' rearranges the letters of ORGANISE REP; 'noted' plays on musical notes as well as fame.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer of opera performs musical notes, so is literally a performer of notes.

clue.text: Sort of restaurant making Greek unwell

parts.note: ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A restaurant's food makes a Greek diner sick.
explanation.definitionFit: A grill is an eatery specialising in grilled food, so a type of restaurant.

clue.text: Clever researcher? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the word researcher is used

explanation.surface: A researcher is described as only partly clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means slyly knowing or cunning, close to clever.

clue.text: Newspaper editor was angry

parts.note: a rag is a slang term for a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper's editor was furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Raged means stormed with fury, the past tense matching was angry.

clue.text: Plant provided by fellow Scotsman

parts.note: a gent is a man or fellow
Ian is a typical Scottish first name, the Scots form of John

explanation.surface: A Scottish man supplies a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain flower, often deep blue, found in alpine regions.

clue.text: Innkeeper resettled in the Loire

indicators.note: resettled means moved to a new place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An innkeeper has moved to the Loire valley in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs a hotel is a modern innkeeper.

clue.text: Feature of crossword that's oddly cultured

indicators.note: oddly means take the letters in odd-numbered positions of the word cultured

explanation.surface: A crossword is said to have a quality that is strangely refined.
explanation.definitionFit: Every crossword is made of these hints that lead the solver to each entry.
